posts.name: McBehrer
posts.cooked:
I don’t know who Leo is, but DAMN that was a good trap. I didn’t even see it until it was too late! (Almost.)

Major Flay makes villain Ongoing cards indestructible, and Unshackled Destinies made it so fatal damage for ANYONE was impossible.

Eventually I finished them all off on one fell swoop, using End of Days to take everyone out and blowing up an Explosives Wagon to kill the villains. I did make one mistake, which was not killing all of the agents before setting off the bombs, so I had to undo to save the game. Would have been a mint otherwise, though.

posts.cooked: Mint by the skin of my teeth.  I spotted the trap while reviewing the opening cards.  I considered just letting it stick around and protect the heroes, but I decided that Miss Information had too many Ongoings that prevented the heroes from dealing damaget to villians, and chucked Major Flay at Fright Train at the earliest opportunity.  Things rapidly turned into massive explodey damage.  The Arsonist set off the Explosives Wagon (which makes sense, I suppose), and when the dust had settled only Mr. Fixer, Sergant Steel and the Arsonist himself were still standing.  Mr. Fixer was at 1, but he used Mantis Style to survive Sustain the Portal, Fright Train's incap damage, FILTER's attacks, and finally the Hayes brother with the machine gun, only for Steel to get shot by the Sheriff.

posts.name: scifantasy
posts.cooked:
Fine, after way too many tries. This was just not gelling for me.

What ended up working was taking advantage of the Unshackled Flay Combo to dump all of Visionary’s damage to an indestructible Decoy Projection, including all the high-powered Fright Train attacks, while I set up with Fanatic. When the time was right, it was a Final Dive to take out Flay while Twisted Reality was in play, and then with the second card, a Consecrated Ground to clear out Internal Collapse, and the three damage plinks cleared Unshackled by consequence, then Espionagent, then I took out the Wagon. The cascade of damage cleared Steel’s squad and piled harder on the villains than me (especially because, as discussed, Visionary was at full health), so it was all over but the shouting. Then the shouting was done too.

posts.name: Melkhor
posts.cooked:
Mint for me, thanks to a very, very lucky reshuffle. I blew up the Explosive Wagon before realising that the Espionagent would make Steel and his rapidly growing crew immune, and was afraid I'd really dug myself into a hole because of it. But then Miss Information was kind enough to reshuffle Fanatic's hand and provide her with 4 new cards, one of them being Wrathful Retribution. Doing some quick math in my head to be sure, I confirmed that Fanatic had 8 HP left, 4 cards in hand and that Steel was at exactly 21 HP.... and suddenly, I didn't have an Agent problem any longer!

Sadly, Fanatic herself went down almost immediately afterwards, but Fixer carried the fight the rest of the way with some very timely damage deflection from Mantis style. A point of particular hilarity occured when he finished off Miss Information by deflecting the start of turn damage from Steel's incap effect from Fright Train, due to the Nemesis bonus!

Who knew that being Bunker's Nemesis was such a competitive field?

posts.cooked:
Mint, but barely.  I won with only Mr Fixer left standing at 2hp.

Spotted the trap late as I failed to think the combination all the way through (causing me to waste a couple of cards and lost the Pipe Wrench that I thought would be safe).  Managed to get and recycle Grease Gun a couple times to keep damage low, but mistimed the Final Dive to take out Flay so that I ended up having to eat a lot of damage from the exploding wagon.  Thankfully, that wiped most of the field anyway and I was able to protect Fixer long enough to take out Fright Train for the win.

Great One Shot.  This one really felt like a puzzle rather than a random game of the week and highlighted some neat interactions.
